config.server.path.description: Absolute path to a `qbx-lua-ls` binary. Leave empty to use the one bundled with the extension.
config.library.description: Extra folders to index for definitions, for example a `resources` folder that contains `ox_lib` and `qbx_core` when you only open a single resource. Resources referenced from `fxmanifest.lua` that sit next to the open one are found automatically.
config.diagnostics.enable.description: Show Qbox Lua diagnostics while editing.
config.diagnostics.workspace.description: Report problems for every Lua file in the workspace in the Problems panel, not only for the files that are open.
config.diagnostics.rules.description: Rule levels, e.g. `{ "unused-argument": "off", "fivem/citizen-prefix": "warning" }`. The levels a `qbxlint.toml` in the workspace sets take precedence, so the editor and CI stay in sync.
config.diagnostics.strict.description: Also report what TypeScript's strict mode does beyond lua-language-server: `need-check-nil` for arithmetic, concatenation, `#` and comparisons with a value that may be `nil`, the `nil` of fields, optional callback parameters and other functions in `param-type-mismatch`, `field = nil` for fields that do not allow it, the fields of shapes in `missing-fields`, and fields of tables built by table constructors in `inject-field` and `undefined-field`. A `strict` that a `qbxlint.toml` in the workspace sets takes precedence.
config.inlayHints.enable.description: Show parameter names next to literal arguments.
config.semanticTokens.enable.description: Colour natives, globals, parameters and methods semantically.
config.sqlHighlighting.enable.descriptio: Highlight SQL in the queries of database calls such as `MySQL.query.await(...)`, in calls of functions whose first parameter has the `sql` type, and in strings below `---@language sql`. Takes effect after the window reloads, for every window.
config.hover.verbosity.description: How much a hover shows when it opens: `0` the type alone, `1` also the fields of tables and the aliases they use, and each level up to `5` more fields and one more step of the tables and classes they hold. The `+` and `-` buttons of a hover show more or less of that hover.
config.hover.rememberVerbosity.descripti: Open hovers at the level last chosen with the `+` and `-` buttons of a hover instead of `#qbxLua.hover.verbosity#`, also after a restart. Changing either setting starts again from `#qbxLua.hover.verbosity#`.
config.mapViewer.xmlFiles.description: How `.ymap` and `.ytyp` files that contain XML text open. Binary map files always open in the map viewer.
config.mapViewer.xmlFiles.enum.text: Open XML map files in the text editor. The map viewer stays available from the editor title bar and the Explorer menu.
config.mapViewer.xmlFiles.enum.viewer: Open XML map files in the map viewer, like binary ones.
config.assets.nameLists.description: Absolute paths of name lists the asset viewers use to turn hashes back into names, for example a text file with one base-game object name per line. Text, INI and JSON files work: every identifier in them is tried. Names of asset files in the same resource are always used. **FiveM: Add Asset Name List** adds files here.
config.warnAboutOtherLuaExtensions.descr: Warn when another Lua language server extension is active, which leads to duplicate diagnostics and completions.
config.trace.server.description: Trace the communication between VS Code and the language server.

walkthrough.gettingStarted.title: Get started with Qbox Lua for FiveM

walkthrough.gettingStarted.reference.des:
Natives, controls, ped flags, snippets and hashes are a command away.
[Open FiveM Reference](command:qbxLua.openReference)
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: Lua language features, the reference and the map, model, texture and animation viewers work in Restricted Mode. Resource control, the NUI preview, the assistant tools and a custom server path or library need a trusted workspace.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces.descripti: The language server and the resource tools read files from the local disk.
